subject: Throughput sizing & SLO follow-up (FinEx) - post-call recap
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput sizing & SLO follow-up (FinEx) - post-call recap

Hi Sam, thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same assumptions: 

What we heard from FinEx:
- Primary use: real-time summarization of intra-day trading notes and alerts, surfaced in dashboards.
- Streaming required: client needs first-token streaming (partial transcripts) and incremental updates for UI.
- Target latency: p95 first-token <= 250 ms (preferably <=200 ms); end-to-end response p95 <= 600 ms for full output.
- Throughput/Concurrency:
  - Steady-state: ~25 QPS (concurrent sessions ~150)
  - Daily peak window (09:30\u201310:15 ET): sustained 550 QPS, short bursts to ~1,200 QPS for 30\u201390s
  - Average request size: prompt ~60 tokens, response ~180 tokens (avg total ~240 tokens)
- Tokenization/Model: currently evaluating a 13B open model; will confirm whether they need FP16 or 8-bit quantized variant.
- KV cache usage: sessions are short-lived (<= 60s) so KV cache hit is low, but they rely on context windows up to 2k tokens.

Attachments: Sam said he would share workload extracts \u2014 I referenced where to upload in the Drive link below.

Next steps (owners):
- Sam / FinEx: share the detailed workload CSV with per-minute QPS for the past 30 days + latency targets (action: FinEx) \u2014 due by Thu 9/16.
- Rafael: review sizing numbers and propose Dedicated/Duo cluster sizing options + cost delta for quantized vs FP16 (action: Rafael) \u2014 tentative by Mon 9/20.
- Marissa: prepare a streaming/first-token demo runbook and an example baseline config (action: Marissa).
- Neha: schedule follow-up call to review sizing and canary plan (action: Neha).

If any of these recap points are off, flag them and I'll correct. Otherwise I'll expect the CSV and we'll run the sizing exercise.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[attachment: finex_meeting_notes.txt (text/plain)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing & SLO follow-up (FinEx) - post-call recap

Thanks Neha \u2014 good notes. A couple internal clarifications before we size: 

Questions for FinEx we should confirm in the CSV or follow-up:
1) Model variant they prefer (13B vs 70B) and whether autoprobing for model fallback is acceptable.
2) Exact definition of "first-token" latency (server acceptance vs network-to-client) \u2014 we size for server-side generation.
3) Percentiles to target: they asked p95; confirm if they also want p99 alerts.
4) Streaming granularity: do they need partial tokens every X ms or every Y tokens? Sam said "snappy" \u2014 need a number (we usually size for 150\u2013300ms chunks).
5) Peak burst profile: length of bursts (30\u201390s noted) \u2014 confirm distribution (we need to know frequency per day).

Assumptions I'll use for an initial sizing run (we can adjust once CSV arrives):
- Model: 13B quantized (8-bit) for baseline; provide FP16 cost for comparison.
- Avg total tokens/request: 240 tokens (prompt+response).
- Steady-state QPS: 25 -> map to concurrency ~150 with avg latency 350ms.
- Peak sustained QPS: 550 -> plan for autoscale group to handle 600QPS sustained, with warm standby to handle bursts to 1.2kQPS for ~60s.
- Streaming: 200ms chunking target.

I'll run a quick back-of-envelope VM/GPU count and send a sizing table once FinEx CSV is in. Rafael

[internal: tagging Rafael for quantization benchmark numbers]

From: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@finex.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinEx Eng Ops <eng-ops@finex.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Throughput sizing & SLO follow-up (FinEx) - post-call recap

Thanks Neha \u2014 attaching the CSV and a short doc with our latency expectations. Key clarifications inline below and in the attached files.

Clarifications: 
- Model: 13B preferred to start; if we see quality gaps we'll evaluate 70B later.
- First-token definition: time from request received by the server to first byte delivered to client (server-side).
- Percentiles: both p95 and p99 are important; p95 is the primary target for user experience, p99 for alerts.
- Streaming: prefer chunks every ~200ms; can tolerate up to 300ms during peaks.
- Burst profile: we see 2\u20133 short bursts per trading day that reach 1k\u20131.4k QPS for 30\u2013120s; sustained peak window is 09:30\u201310:15 ET at ~550 QPS.
- Token details: historical average prompt 58 tokens, avg response 185 tokens (total ~243 tokens). We also included 95th pct response length ~420 tokens.

Files attached:
- finex_workload_profile.csv (per-minute QPS for last 90 days, includes peak annotations)
- finex_latency_targets.pdf (doc with SLA language and p95/p99 targets)

We uploaded a Drive extract here: https://drive.google.com/finex-throughput-profile (same link in your follow-up). Let us know if you need a masked version of the traces.

Thanks \u2014 Sam
Sam Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering | FinEx Capital

Great \u2014 thanks for the quick turnaround and the CSV, Sam. Rafael and I will run the sizing exercise this week using the exact per-minute series; Marissa will stand up a short streaming proof-of-concept to validate first-token targets.

Proposed follow-up call options to go over results and recommended Dedicated sizing:
- Monday 9/20, 10:00am ET
- Tuesday 9/21, 11:00am ET

Please confirm which works and we'll book a calendar invite. We\u2019ll include a preliminary table that shows:
- recommended cluster size for steady-state vs peak (GPU counts and instance types)
- estimated cost delta quantized vs FP16
- canary roll-out plan + rollback criteria (latency/regression thresholds)

Thanks again \u2014 looking forward to the sizing run.

Neha Kapoor
